slides.title: Dryer vent cleaning
slides.body: Property managers carry the fire liability and hate sourcing it. Recurring contract, a van, and about $400 of tools.

slides.title: Post-construction cleanup
slides.body: Small contractors subcontract this on every job and complain about finding anyone reliable. Ask three builders this week.

slides.title: Pool equipment repair
slides.body: Everyone competes on cleaning. Almost nobody does pumps and heaters, which bill at a far higher rate.

slides.title: Menu photography per dish
slides.body: Delivery apps rank listings with photos. Owners know it and still will not shoot them. Price per plate, not per hour.

slides.title: Estate sale listing
slides.body: Heirs will not photograph and list 200 items. You do the work, you take a percentage, they never touch a keyboard.

caption: None of these need a following, an app, or a pitch deck. They need a phone and someone willing to make the first ten calls. Which one would you actually do?

hook: 5 Signs Your Business Idea Is Bad

slides.title: You cannot name one buyer
slides.body: Not a demographic. One person, with a name, who could pay you this week. If they do not exist, neither does the business.

slides.title: Your 'why now' is just AI
slides.body: AI is how you build it, not why anyone needs it. If removing that word kills the pitch, there was no pitch.

slides.title: It needs both sides at once
slides.body: Marketplaces are useless until both sides show up. You are signing up for two businesses, not one.

slides.title: The pitch needs a diagram
slides.body: If you cannot say it in one sentence, a stranger scrolling past will not decode it either.

slides.title: You dread the selling part
slides.body: Excited to build, dreading to sell, is the most common way this ends. Selling is the job.

caption: Most ideas do not fail because they were wrong. They fail because nobody stress-tested them for an afternoon first. Which of these have you been ignoring?

hook: 5 Truths About Starting No One Says

slides.title: Your idea is not the moat
slides.body: Willingness to do sales is. Two people with the same idea get completely different outcomes for this reason alone.

slides.title: First customers already know you
slides.body: They come from your contacts, not from ads. Ads are for scaling something that already converts.

slides.title: You will change it in 60 days
slides.body: Plan for the pivot instead of pretending it will not happen. Build the cheap version you can afford to throw away.

slides.title: Revenue before logo
slides.body: Naming, branding and a website are procrastination wearing a suit. Take money first.

slides.title: Money changing hands is the only proof
slides.body: Not compliments. Not sign-ups. Not 'I would definitely use that.' Only payment.

caption: Every one of these is obvious in hindsight and ignored in practice. Save this and reread it the week you launch. Which one stings the most?
